clue.text: Rustle up new business behind County Court

indicators.note: behind means following, so new business comes after the county abbreviation

parts.note: Co. is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: A lawyer drums up fresh work from the County Court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' places new business after County; 'County Court' reads as one legal body but splits into two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To rustle up a meal or a scheme is to improvise it, which is exactly to concoct it.

clue.text: Rascal moving houses thus caught offering outdated conveyance

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the rearranged letters hold the next part
moving means the letters of rascal shift around

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A rascal caught removing furniture in an old vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' turns RASCAL into CLASAR, which 'houses' SIC + C.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic car is an old vintage motor, a conveyance whose design is out of date.

clue.text: State upset Queen's brief

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards
brief means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: Regina is Latin for queen

explanation.surface: The Queen is upset by a brief state matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts REGINA to REGIN, which 'upset' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a sovereign nation in West Africa, a country or state.

clue.text: Fearful Roe v Wade could be overturned?

indicators.note: overturned signals the letters are upset into a new order

explanation.surface: Nervous speculation that the US abortion ruling might be reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: Roe v Wade was the US Supreme Court ruling overturned in 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overawed is to be cowed by fear or respect, so it means fearful.

clue.text: Demurral over VAT

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned over, reading the letters upwards

parts.note: a but is an objection or demurral

explanation.surface: An objection to value added tax.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT looks like the tax; it is a large container.
explanation.definitionFit: A vat is a large vessel for liquids, like a tub.

clue.text: Contract lawyers make a profit

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers
to gain is to make a profit

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that lawyers turn every contract into money.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is an agreement between parties settling terms, a synonym of a contract.

clue.text: Soul singer needing Chitty on Contracts

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first part above the second

parts.note: a chitty is a chit, a bill; Chitty on Contracts is also an English legal textbook
withers means shrinks or contracts

explanation.surface: A soul star needs a standard contract-law textbook.
explanation.walkthrough: Chitty on Contracts is the classic English textbook on contract law.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Withers was an American soul musician famous for Ain't No Sunshine.

clue.text: Browser showing contents of Green Book, omitting nothing

indicators.note: the contents of a word are the letters inside its ends
omitting means one letter is left out

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone browsing a Green Book catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browser' is not a web reader but an animal that grazes on leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The reebok is a South African antelope that browses on vegetation.

clue.text: US objects first to arraigning criminal in camera

indicators.note: the first letter of a word
criminal suggests wrongly arranged letters

explanation.surface: An American objects to a defendant being tried in private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In camera' is the legal term for a hearing held in private.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana are artefacts typical of American culture, objects from the US.

clue.text: Heading north is popular, depending on conditions at court

indicators.note: heading north in a down clue means reading upwards

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Going north depends on the conditions at court.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree nisi takes effect unless a condition intervenes, so it depends on conditions.

clue.text: University dons rage about quibble

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the rearranged word is worn around the university letter
about signals the letters of rage are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Academics fly into a fury over some petty point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like the noun for lecturers; it is the verb putting ARGE (the anagram of RAGE, from 'about') around U.
explanation.definitionFit: To quibble is to raise petty objections, which is a mild way to dispute or debate.

clue.text: The faithful priest in the case of Beebe v HM Customs, removing habit

indicators.note: in places the priest within the shell of the following name
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword regular
v is short for versus, kept as the letter
Her Majesty is ER, Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: removing takes the second word out of the first

parts.note: customs are habits, established practices
habit, singular, is the part taken away

explanation.surface: A legal report of a faith case: Beebe versus HM Customs, about a nun's habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' takes HABIT from HABITS, leaving S. The whole surface is a mock law-report title.
explanation.definitionFit: The faithful are religious people, those who hold a belief.

clue.text: Better almost certainly to say nothing when questioned

indicators.note: almost means the word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: sure means certainly, as in 'sure, I'll come'
in a quiz you say 'pass' when you will not answer

explanation.surface: Advice that it is wiser to keep silent under interrogation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SURE to SUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To better something is to outdo or exceed it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Skimpy trousers Henry split giving waspish summary judgment

parts.note: shorts are short trousers
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
a rift is a split

explanation.surface: Henry splits his short trousers and gets a curt reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: Short shrift means brusque, dismissive treatment, a sharp hasty dismissal.

clue.text: Meet your maker after court — it's the gallows

indicators.note: after places the dying part following the courting part

parts.note: to court is to woo
to meet your maker is a euphemism for dying

explanation.surface: A grim sentence: after the trial in court comes death on the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court; it is the verb meaning to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodie is an old Scots word for the gallows, a crossword-friendly dialect term.

clue.text: Details probably missed in dash around shopping centre

indicators.note: around means the run is placed round the shops

parts.note: a sprint is a dash
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: Things overlooked while racing round a mall.
explanation.definitionFit: Small print is the fine detail in a contract that readers usually overlook.

clue.text: Donut and coke supply failed

indicators.note: supply is read as the adverb from supple, loosely, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: The stock of doughnuts and cola ran out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun; it is an adverb (supplely) signalling the anagram of DONUT and COKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Conked out is slang for broke down or stopped working, so it means failed.

clue.text: Location for Wendy house reflected equal right to light

indicators.note: reflected means mirrored, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: even means equal
to light is to land, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: A legal right to light for a Wendy house, a children's playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' is the verb, to come to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: In Peter Pan, Wendy goes to the island where the Lost Boys build her a house.

clue.text: Affectionate women are mostly married

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A sweeping statement that women tend to be married.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm person shows friendliness and love, so warm is a synonym of affectionate.

clue.text: Murderer's impertinence when in jails

indicators.note: jails means locks up, so the outer words hold the cheek

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
sass is cheek or impertinence

explanation.surface: A killer's cheek when in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jails' looks like a noun of the prison scene; it is the verb, the outer words locking up the cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a killer of a prominent person.

clue.text: Carton's inside around five wanting a bit of tea — that's Sydney's afternoon!

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken away
around puts the inner letters of the box round the Roman numeral
the inside of a word is all its letters except the two ends

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: a bit of the word tea is just its first letter

explanation.surface: An Australian taking an afternoon cup of tea from a carton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' gives ARTO from CARTON; V goes in after AR, and 'wanting' drops the T. 'Sydney' stands for any Australian.
explanation.definitionFit: Arvo is Australian slang for the afternoon, so Sydney's afternoon is a fitting regional pointer.

clue.text: Opening for legal trainees involved being shelled on a plane?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A legal training vacancy and a creature under fire on an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' mixes TRAINEES; the plane is the plane tree, not an aircraft, and 'shelled' means having a shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree snail is a creature with a shell that lives on trees, such as a plane tree.

clue.text: Mr Universe repeatedly lifts small submarine, perhaps

indicators.note: lifts means holds up, so in a down clue the small letter sits on top

parts.note: Arnold Schwarzenegger, Arnie, won the Mr Universe title several times

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder lifting a mini submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: A sarnie is British slang for a sandwich; a submarine is a long sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine is a long filled roll, an example of a sandwich.

clue.text: Force open commonplace letter for barrister in the Strand

indicators.note: in places the letter within the shore word

parts.note: a strand is a beach; the Strand is also the London street of the Royal Courts of Justice
the commonest letter in barrister is R, which appears three times

explanation.surface: Breaking into a barrister's chambers on London's Strand, home of the main civil courts.
explanation.definitionFit: To breach a wall or defence is to break through it, which is forcing it open.

clue.text: Second drudge like Rumpole maybe happy to share chambers

parts.note: a hack is a drudge; Rumpole of the Bailey, the TV barrister, calls himself an Old Bailey hack
up means cheerful or happy

explanation.surface: A junior barrister is glad to share chambers with a Rumpole-type veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumpole is the fictional barrister of the British TV series Rumpole of the Bailey.
explanation.definitionFit: To shack up is slang for living together, sharing rooms; chambers are both rooms and barristers' offices.

clue.text: Jack pukes in the Middle Temple's central area

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its centre letter

parts.note: the nave is the main central part of a church or temple

explanation.surface: Jack vomits in the Middle Temple, one of London's Inns of Court.
explanation.walkthrough: The Middle Temple is one of London's four Inns of Court for barristers.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave is the jack in a deck of playing cards.

clue.text: Spring, time for dispute

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Spring is the season for quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel or minor dispute.

clue.text: Litigious patent-holder, in patent dispute?

parts.note: patent as an adjective means obvious or plain
a tiff is a minor quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: A patent owner suing in a patent case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patent' first means a licence, then the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the party who brings a lawsuit, so a patent-holder who sues is one.

clue.text: Pro bono clinic offers sandwiches on the turn

indicators.note: on the turn means reversing, so the letters read backwards
sandwiches means holds between, so the letters lie inside these words

explanation.surface: A free legal clinic hands out sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters COF lie in 'clinic offers' and 'on the turn' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro bono work is done without payment, the abbreviation for free of charge.

clue.text: Police force remains independent but close to judiciary

indicators.note: but means except, so the letter is left out

parts.note: remains, the verb, means stays

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A police force that stays independent apart from links to the judges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' takes the Y (close to judiciary) out of STAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stasi was the secret police of East Germany.

clue.text: Most orderly trial with papers I lodged

indicators.note: lodged means placed inside, so the papers and I go into the trial word

parts.note: a test is a trial
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A tidy trial in which I lodged my documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiest is the superlative of tidy, meaning neatest or best arranged.

clue.text: Prisoner delighted to give permission for it?

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
sent is slang for thrilled or delighted

explanation.surface: A convict is thrilled to be allowed something.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'it' is sex.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent is to agree to or allow something.
